faq_title: Questions we get asked about double-column band saws

faq.q: Why choose a double-column saw over a pivot saw?
faq.a: Rigidity and capacity. The bow is guided on two columns, so there is no side load on the blade — cuts stay square in large solids and the blade lasts longer. Double-column saws also reach capacities a pivot bow cannot: 330 mm up to 1500 mm on the Bekamak range.

faq.q: Can a double-column saw cut miters?
faq.a: Yes — the BMSY CGH (single miter) and BMSY DG NC (double miter) swivel the whole bow assembly up to 60° under hydraulic or NC control, and the automatic CGS/CDGS NC models do the same with servo feeding.
The SV versions of the BMSY C saws have a second vise jaw close to the blade, so short pieces and remnants are clamped on both sides of the cut — useful for cutting slices from blocks and billets.
Bekamak's high-tech production saws: servo-driven bow feed and material feed, full enclosure and CNC control, designed for carbide blades, the fastest cycle times and unattended running.
